problem:
The displacement $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ of mass $4\,\text{kg}$ is given by

$$
r=⟨6{t}^{3/2},\,{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}⟩,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the resultant force acting on the particle when $t=4\,\text{s}.$

activity_context.topic_title: Applying Newton's Second Law in the Plane

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Resultant Force Acting on a Particle Given Its Displacement Vector
examples.problem:
The displacement $\mathbf r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ of mass $3\,\textrm{kg}$ is given by

$$
\mathbf r =  \langle 3\cos{t}-\sin{t},\: 2\cos{t}\rangle,
$$

where $t\gt 0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the resultant force acting on the particle when $t=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\,\textrm s.$
examples.worked_solution:
Newton’s second law states that

$$
\mathbf F = m \mathbf a,
$$

 
where $\mathbf F$ is the *resultant* force, $m$ is the mass, and $\mathbf a$ is the acceleration.

To compute the acceleration vector, we first differentiate $\mathbf r$ to get the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate the velocity vector to get the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the resultant force $\mathbf F$ at time $t$ equals

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =3\cdot ⟨-3\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡t-9\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-6\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when $t = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}\,\textrm s,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(\frac{3\pi }{4}) & =⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4})-9\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}),\,-6\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}+\frac{9\sqrt{2}}{2},\,\frac{6\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨6\sqrt{2},\,3\sqrt{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the resultant force acting on $P$ when $t=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\,\textrm s$ equals $\left\langle 6\sqrt{2},\: 3\sqrt{2}\right\rangle\,\textrm N.$

feedback.problem:
The velocity $v,$ in meters per second, of a particle $P$ of mass $6\,\text{kg}$ is given by

$$
v=⟨3\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-4),\,\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}⟩,
$$

where $t>4$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the resultant force acting on the particle when $t=7\,\text{s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Newton’s second law states that

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the *resultant* force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-4)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{t-4},\,t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the resultant force $F$ at time $t$ equals

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =6\cdot ⟨\frac{3}{t-4},\,t⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{18}{t-4},\,6t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when $t=7\,\text{s},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(7) & =⟨\frac{18}{7-4},\,6(7)⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,42⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the resultant force acting on $P$ when $t=7\,\text{s}$ equals $⟨6,\,42⟩\,\text{N}.$
